Title: Dreams and Dreamsicles: A Story of Nighttime Delights

In the quiet town of Duskville, nestled between the fringes of the sky where it meets the earth under a blanket of stars, there lived a boy named Ferdinand. Ferdinand had a unique fascination with the night - something that fascinated him more than any object, any book, or any adventure could. The whimsical way the town shimmied into slumber was something Ferdinand had learned to dance with, navigating through the night with grace.

One evening, under the light of a full moon, Ferdinand invited his best friend, Olive, to venture into the dense forest that fronted the town. It was a mysterious place, full of secrets and tall tales. Ferdinand smiled and whispered, "It's like trying to find our dreams, in each other's company."

The forest was dark, with only the moon as their guiding light. Ferdinand guided the way, knowing every turn and feature of the forest as if it were a map he had been learning since childhood. They stepped over stream beds, over roots, and around moss-covered boulders, each step bringing them closer to the fabric of their shared dreams.

Suddenly, Olive stopped in her tracks. In front of her, basking in the silvery glow of the moon, was a bundle of sticks. With great trepidation, now wide-eyed with curiosity, Olive approached the bundle. Ferdinand came to stand by her side, half-expecting to see the Hat Man, the reason children her age feared the forest.

"Do you have any idea?" Olive asked, holding the bundle in her hands. "Do you think these are dreams?"

"I think you're about to find out," Ferdinand replied, spinning a tale that had been in his mind ever since he learned the art of finding dreams.

They then gathered the sticks together, and producing a bottle he'd never seen before from one of his pockets, Ferdinand asked the accursed hat man hanging upside down on one of the branches for something called "Dreamsicles."

As magic flooded from the bottle, the sticks began to move in unseen currents. Pieces of them broke off and floated through the air. When they caught the pieces, the children put them into a cauldron.

However, as soon as Ferdinand reached for the last piece, Olive jerked her hand back. "Wait, there's one more!" First, she waited, and then out of nowhere appeared what seemed to be the most genuine dreamstick ever, accompanied by vivid mental images that made their eyes tear up with joy. Beneath the moonlight, they chanted to transform it into a dreamstick, and it looked like it came straight from the beatific ecstasy of a dream made manifest.

As soon as the chant reached completion, the dreamstick began to glow with a bright, ethereal light. In a moment, it had become something else entirely. But it was now a dreamstick, indeed.

The story of Dreamwalking came from this event and spread among the villagers. Now, every night, in the quiet corners of their homes, children from Duskville stood on the banks of the Dawn River holding the glowing dreamstick, and with a whispered secret chant, they dreamwalked with Ferdinand and Olive into the realms of their collective dreams.

Months passed, and the dreamwalking ritual was the talk of the town during the day. It became so popular that dreams became more tangible, and the children who had no vision could see the world of dreams under fluorescent lights. Sleep no longer bore the torment of forgetfulness, and the children's parents thanked the boys for teaching them how to embrace the world they had spent their nights trying to fathom.

But all was not entirely rosy. Ferdinand was enervated by the need to live among the dreams of his friends. One day, he decided it was time to explore the dreams of Duskville on his own terms.

As he walked, an untouchable, in his reflections, he encountered the same kind of abyss that supposedly claimed visiting dreamers. A voice, not his own, piped up, "Don't you see? Between me and the Innermost Dream, there's simply nothing. I've never known fear, not because I've not felt it, but because I've somehow grown immune to it."

In this abyss, Ferdinand understood the need to honor the Duskville dreamwalkers' plea to never take it for granted. But the truth stayed with him, and he didn't understand how he could forge his own path without the dreams of his friends to guide him.

One day, as fate would have it, he met a woman named Eleanor, a dreamwalker herself, who had developed a fascination for exploring the nights with eyes of other dreamers. They formed a bond, unbound by the necessity to share whispered chants or mundanely goblin-encumbered forest scaretales. Together, they continued to dreamwalk, unlocking the dreams of children from other corners of the world. Sure enough, Eleanor recognized the need to continue this legacy and inspired Ferdinand to come back to Duskville.

Ferdinand returned, but now the bond between him and Duskville was different. He had become a dreamwalker in his own right, the origin of the Guild of Nightmembers, intertwining his powers with the mystique he had inherited from Oliver and himself. He brought back the dreamstalks and the magic, and allowed Duskville to flourish.

The Guild of Nightmembers became known worldwide. The legends of their lives were ethereally passed down, weaving stories of exploration, empathy, and the personified encapsulation of dreams worldwide.

Towards the end of the tale, Ferdinand was stricken with a vision. He saw himself at the edge of towns, holding the dreamstalk, and speaking to children he didn't know. "Remember," he said, "our dreams are indistinguishable from that of any other. However, we owe a duty to the story that dreams can be vibrant and practical. The Nightmember meets both sides of the Moon and creates stories to blend them."

The story closes with Ferdinand ensuring that the bridge does not fall. He and Eleanor agree that any night meeting must ensure that Duskville is never left behind in shadow, always sings of a starlight.

And so, in the quiet town of Duskville, amidst the fringes of the sky that meets the earth under a blanket of stars, legends are born in the dream, and in the dream, stories like no other begin their tale. The dream itself is the destination, and there are no limits to where the Night Members and the dreamwalkers can take it. 

"Duskville has become renowned across the world," Ferdinand once said during a dreamwalk, "Not because it was its light that I saw, but because I saw, not just a town, but a world glowing through the veil of the night."

From the depth of the unconscious to the edges of space and time, the night to the day, the essence of dreams flourishes and grows, pulling children from every realm together. And what started as a nostalgia for Ferdinand's dream under the stars had evolved into the entire world dreaming together.
